items.summary_en:
Too many VCs are chasing dopamine.. or rage baiting purposely just to get more views on this platform. 

X is not for nuance, so once you say something, you really can't take it back. 

I don't think they understand how it's actually destroying their long term brand. Unfortunately, it hurts the people "under" them more than the person talking. 

Case in point, I know of two folks who lost deals that were all set because of the drama going on X. 

Given how much a commodity "capital" actually is and the sheer number of venture funds, you'd think people would be smarter than this. 

But in this era of wanting airtime, I guess very few are playing long term games.

items.author: Aaron Levie
items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
Cyber will be one of the most defining domains for AI in the coming years, and a huge area of focus for most enterprises.

AI is going to now create a whole new level of work for security dealing with the increase of vibe coded issues, agentic attacks, and even accidental agent swarms hunting for data. OpenAI + Hugging Face is just a preview of what’s to come.

Security teams have often been the most strapped for resources teams in the enterprise, and now it’s only going to get more intense. AI agents of course become the solution to this problem as well, and we’ll see a range of new agentic products for protecting code, enterprise systems, mission critical infrastructure, and enterprise data. Huge opportunity here right now.

And it’s going to be a booming market for cyber professionals that can effectively deploy agents for security purposes in the enterprise. Great time to be in security.
items.summary_zh: 网络安全会成为 AI 时代最关键、也最吃紧的战场：vibe coding 漏洞、智能体攻击、误触发的 agent 群都会把企业安全团队压到极限。真正的机会在于用 AI agent 反过来守代码、系统、关键基础设施和数据，能把 agent 部署进企业安全的人会迎来一波大行情。

items.author: Boris Cherny
items.bio: Claude Code @anthropicai
items.summary_en:
I am surprised that people are surprised this is how I prompt Claude.

Talk to Claude the way you would a coworker. There's no secret to prompting. There's no need to be overly scaffolded or prescriptive for most tasks -- give Claude a goal, and it will figure it out.

Back in the Sonnet 3.5 days, your prompt mattered a lot. Nowadays, it's much more important to communicate to the model:

1. What you want it to do
2. How much effort you want it to spend
3. How it should verify that it did the right thing
items.summary_zh: 别再把提示词当玄学了：像跟同事说话一样给 Claude 一个目标，它会自己搞定。现在真正重要的不是精雕细琢 prompt，而是说清楚你要什么、要它花多少力气、怎么验证结果对不对。

items.author: Unsupervised Learning
items.title: Ep 94: Applied Compute CEO on the Limits of RL, the New AI Hyperscaler & Why Post-Training Wins Inference
items.summary_en:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:02
How do you kind of characterize where we are today?

Speaker 2 | 00:02 - 00:25
What we have with RL is we essentially have a hill climbing machine. The hardest part is actually defining the hill to climb, which is why evals, I think, is like a really important thing for companies to, a, focus on building and b, actually like safeguard pretty carefully. Your employees are not fungible. You would not like be comfortable with them going to another company and doing work there. And same thing with these models.

Speaker 1 | 00:29 - 01:07
Owning your own intelligence and training your own models is incredibly in the AI zeitgeist these days. There's probably no better person to speak with about all these topics than Josh from Applied Compute. Applied Compute is working with a bunch of the most cutting edge AI applications on a really interesting post training examples. Josh and I were able to talk about his perspective on a bunch of the top questions around open models today, including when it actually makes sense to post train these models, how to think about the future of when this stuff makes sense, especially as the labs, you know, get more and more data from different domains over time. We also talked about, like, when it makes sense to harness optimize versus actually go and post train, as well as just get Yash's thoughts on a lot of the really interesting things happening in the ecosystem today.

Speaker 1 | 01:07 - 01:18
All in all, it's a fascinating conversation with a brilliant mind in the space. I hope folks enjoyed as much as I did. Without further ado, here's Yacht. Well, thanks so much for for coming on the podcast.

Speaker 2 | 01:18 - 01:19
Thank you for having me.

Speaker 1 | 01:19 - 01:22
Yeah. Been looking forward to this one for
items.summary_zh: RL 本质上是爬山机器，真正难的是定义要爬哪座山，所以 evals 会变成公司必须重点建设、严密保护的核心资产。员工不是可替换零件，模型也一样，不能训练完就假装谁都能拿去用。
